message.content:
**Proteins that are commonly found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Typical Function | Representative Examples | |----------|------------------|-------------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; often serve as channels, transporters, or receptors. | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (ion pump)
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** (facilitated diffusion)
• **Aquaporin‑4** (water channel)
• **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** – e.g., β‑adrenergic receptor, rhodopsin
• **Ionotropic glutamate receptors** (e.g., NMDA receptor)
• **Voltage‑gated ion channels** – e.g., Na⁺, K⁺, Ca²⁺ channels
• **Connexins** (gap‑junction hemichannels)
• **Integrins** (cell‑matrix adhesion)
• **Cadherins** (cell‑cell adhesion)
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases** – e.g., EGFR, HER2 | | **Peripheral membrane proteins** | Associate with the membrane surface (inner or outer leaflet) via electrostatic or lipid‑anchor interactions. | • **Ankyrin** (links integral proteins to the cytoskeleton)
• **Spectrin** (provides membrane stability)
• **Actin‑binding proteins** – e.g., profilin, cofilin
• **Src family kinases** (membrane‑associated signaling)
• **GPI‑anchored proteins** – e.g., CD59, prion protein (GPI‑anchored to the outer leaflet) | | **Lipid‑anchored proteins** | Covalently attached to lipids (e.g., farnesyl, geranylgeranyl, palmitoyl) that embed them in the membrane. | • **Ras** (farnesylated)
• **Rho** (geranylgeranylated)
• **Src** (myristoylated & palmitoylated) | | **Cholesterol‑binding proteins** | Interact with membrane cholesterol to modulate fluidity and signaling. | • **Stomatin** (cholesterol‑binding integral protein)
• **Flotillin** (lipid‑raft marker) | ### How to use this list - **Research**: If you’re studying a particular signaling pathway, look for the relevant GPCRs, RTKs, or ion channels listed above. - **Biochemistry**: When purifying membrane fractions, these proteins are typical targets for assays (e.g., Western blotting for Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase or EGFR). - **Cell biology**: Understanding the roles of peripheral proteins (ankyrin, spectrin) helps explain membrane mechanics and cytoskeletal organization. Feel free to ask for more details on any specific protein family or for a deeper dive into their structure‑function relationships!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are the names of proteins found in the plasma membrane?" They want a list of proteins found in the plasma membrane. We can provide a general answer: types of proteins: integral membrane proteins (e.g., ion channels, transporters, receptors), peripheral membrane proteins (e.g., cytoskeletal proteins, signaling proteins). Provide examples: e.g., Na+/K+ ATPase, GLUT1, G-protein coupled receptors, integrins, cadherins, connexins, etc. Also mention peripheral proteins like actin-binding proteins, ankyrin, spectrin. Provide a concise but comprehensive list. No function calls needed.
